text.p: Sterling surged in Europe, boosted by firm oil prices and a record high for UK stocks, hitting a 21-month high on the mark and 11-month peaks versus the dollar.
Dealers said promising UK economic fundamentals, which boosted the FTSE share index to an all-time high, were having a knock-on effect on the pound.

"The rise in oil prices could provide an additional boost to Europe's petro-currencies, the pound and the Norwegian crown, even if this boost is more apparent than real in the case of sterling," said Paul Meggyesi of Deutche Morgan Grenfell.

Sterling comfortably overcame the 2.42 mark hurdle and powered through the next resistance level of 2.4230. At 0901 GMT it was trading at 2.4270/75, way above late Monday's European level of 2.4160/65.
The pound was also bullish against the dollar, breaking through $1.5830 before pulling back a touch to $1.5825/32. It closed at $1.5802/12 yesterday.
A strong session in Asia extended sterling's gains against the yen, although late sales trimmed some strength. It was trading at 177.30/58 yen at 0902 GMT.

Britain's detachment from the debate over European economic and monetary union (EMU) provided respite for dealers nervous about the continuing uncertainties of entry surrounding other European currencies.
Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said Britain's wait-and-see attitude to EMU was to be regretted.
Speaking at a meeting organised by the Hamburg saving bank, Krupp said, "It is to be regretted that Britain and Sweden have decided to forego obligatory membership of monetary union."
With no major UK data due out until Wednesday's September public sector borrowing requirement and unemployment figures, dealers said the market would remain bullish.
"Apart from some short-term profit-taking, sterling should remain strong for the time being," said a British bank dealer.
Technical analysts said the breach of 2.4230 marks had set sterling on the path to 2.43, with some expecting that goal to be reached as early as today.

"For today we expect 2.43. Medium-term we expect 2.4350 before the end of the week, and then next week we might crash through the 2.44," said Peter Lenzinger, customer adviser at Olsen and Associates in Zurich.
There were warnings, however, that cable could find its energy beginning to wane just beyond current levels, with an intraday top seen likely to form around $1.5840.
"The upside may be somewhat limited with $1.5820/40 resistance to watch for a breakout to $1.5960," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.
